edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. edits.name: Severance clause

edits.text: 4. NON-COMPETE. During employment and for twelve months following termination of employment, the Executive shall not, within any jurisdiction in which the Company conducts material business, directly engage in a business that is competitive with the Company's material products or services, except to the extent such restriction is prohibited or limited by applicable law.
edits.name: Non-compete clause

edits.text: 1. POSITION. The Executive shall serve as Chief Operating Officer and shall perform such duties and responsibilities as are customarily associated with that position and as may reasonably be assigned by the Chief Executive Officer or the Board of Directors. The Executive shall devote substantially all business time and attention to the Company; provided that the Executive may engage in charitable, civic, personal investment, board, advisory, and other outside activities that do not, individually or in the aggregate, create a reasonable conflict of interest with the Company, materially interfere with the Executive's duties, or violate the Executive's confidentiality, non-solicitation, or other restrictive covenant obligations to the Company. The Executive shall provide advance notice to the Company of any outside activity that would reasonably be expected to create such a conflict or interference, and the Company shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay any required consent.
edits.name: Position; permitted outside activities

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive's employment without Cause, and subject to the Executive's execution and non-revocation of a customary release of claims in favor of the Company as described below, the Executive shall be entitled to receive an amount equal to six (6) months of the Executive's then-current annual base salary (the "Severance Amount"), less applicable withholdings and deductions. The Severance Amount shall be paid in substantially equal installments over the six (6)-month period following the termination date in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices, commencing on the first regular payroll date after the release becomes effective and irrevocable; provided that the first payment shall include any installments that would have been paid between the termination date and such first payment date. The Company shall provide the release to the Executive within five (5) business days following the termination date, and the Executive must execute and not revoke the release within the time period specified in the release, which shall not exceed sixty (60) days following the termination date. The Severance Amount shall not be subject to forfeiture based on a general continued-compliance condition; provided, however, that if the Executive materially breaches any confidentiality, non-solicitation, non-disparagement, return-of-property, or other valid post-employment restrictive covenant obligation owed to the Company, and such breach, if capable of cure, remains uncured for ten (10) business days after written notice from the Company reasonably describing the breach, the Company may suspend any unpaid installments of the Severance Amount to the extent permitted by applicable law and without limiting any other remedies available to the Company.
edits.name: Severance entitlement; release mechanics; limited forfeiture standard

edits.text: 4. NON-COMPETE. During employment and, only to the extent enforceable under applicable law, for six (6) months following termination of employment, the Executive shall not, within the Restricted Territory, directly provide services that are the same as or substantially similar to the services the Executive provided to the Company during the twelve (12) months preceding termination to a business line of a competitor that offers products or services that are materially competitive with the Company's products or services for which the Executive had material responsibility or about which the Executive received material confidential information during such twelve (12)-month period. For purposes of this Section, "Restricted Territory" means the specific states, provinces, or metropolitan markets in which the Executive had material operational responsibility on behalf of the Company during the twelve (12) months preceding termination. Nothing in this Section restricts passive ownership of less than two percent (2%) of the outstanding securities of a publicly traded company, employment or service in a non-competitive business unit or function, or activities that would not involve use or disclosure of the Company's confidential information. This Section shall not apply to the extent prohibited or limited by applicable law, including any applicable law restricting non-competition covenants for employees in the relevant jurisdiction, and shall be construed and enforced only to the maximum extent permitted by such law.
edits.name: Narrowed non-compete

receiver.message_back: Thank you—this is close, but to finalize we need two targeted revisions: (i) Section 3 should limit any suspension of severance to a final, non-appealable judicial determination of a material uncured breach of the specifically enumerated obligations, with no suspension for “other” restrictive covenants or alleged non-disparagement absent mutuality; and (ii) Section 4 should be deleted or, at minimum, expressly not apply following a Company termination without Cause or in any jurisdiction where garden leave/consideration or employee non-compete limits would render it unenforceable. With those changes, our client is prepared to sign.
